result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and modern curb ramps with tactile paving, indicating recent infrastructure improvements. However, large utility poles are positioned directly in the middle of the sidewalk path, creating significant obstructions for pedestrians. While a traffic signal is present for vehicles, there are no visible pedestrian-specific signal heads to facilitate safe crossing.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Large wooden utility poles are located in the center of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the effective width and creating a barrier for people with strollers or wheelchairs.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and left side of the sidewalk

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles, but no pedestrian signal heads are visible to indicate when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the furniture zone or underground the utilities to provide a clear, unobstructed pedestrian through-zone.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers and accessible pedestrian signals (APS) to provide clear crossing instructions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Further extend the curb to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and signalized control. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure during crossings.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge or curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Main intersection in the center of the frame

hazards.name: Wide corner radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry on the left allows for higher-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse crosswalk markings to continental or ladder patterns to increase visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on all visible corners, providing basic pedestrian access. However, the environment lacks traffic control signals or signs and has significant sightline obstructions due to parked vehicles near the crossing points.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on both sides of the street are positioned very close to the crosswalk, potentially hiding pedestrians from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both the left and right sides of the main roadway near the intersection.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: No visible stop signs or traffic signals regulate vehicle flow at this multi-leg intersection, increasing the risk of conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection where the crosswalks meet.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalks to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase the prominence of the pedestrian crossing.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a signalized intersection featuring high-visibility zebra crosswalks and a marked bike lane. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the crossing distance is relatively long without a median refuge, and dedicated pedestrian signals are not visible.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes and a bike lane without a midway refuge, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the street to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.
